reasons: Medicine statuses and the 'Remaining' count are invented, which could give a patient wrong information about their doses.
The 'Mark Taken' buttons do not save anything, so the user's action has no effect.

terms.meaning: how closely a patient follows their prescribed medicine schedule
the amount of a medicine to take at one time
a written order from a doctor for a medicine

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the medication card
sections.what: Brings in the React library, icons, the card and button components, and a style helper. Nothing appears on screen from this section.
sections.why: The widget needs these pieces to draw itself.

sections.name: meds
sections.title: Fixed sample medicine list
sections.what: Holds three sample medicines with name, dose, time, a taken flag, and a status of taken, upcoming or missed.
sections.why: Provides sample content so the layout can be seen before real medicine data is connected.
sections.watch_out: These medicines and statuses are invented and must be replaced with real data before any patient relies on them.

sections.name: MedicationWidget (part 1)
sections.title: Medicine rows with status icons
sections.what: Draws a heading and a 'Remaining' count, then one card per medicine with an icon, name, dose, time, and a 'Missed' label when the status is missed.
sections.why: Lets the patient see each medicine's schedule and whether a dose was missed.
sections.watch_out: The 'Remaining' count is fixed at two, so it will not match the list if the data changes.

sections.name: MedicationWidget (part 2)
sections.title: Mark taken buttons and manage link
sections.what: Gives each medicine a 'Mark Taken' button, styled differently when the medicine is taken or upcoming, and a 'Manage Prescriptions' button at the bottom. None of these buttons has a click action in the code.
sections.why: Sets up the layout for the real action of recording doses.
sections.watch_out: Pressing a button shows no result and saves nothing, so the buttons must be wired up before users can rely on them.

summary: A dashboard card that lists three medicines with taken or missed status, but the medicines and their statuses are fixed sample data in the code.
purpose: Shows a daily medicine checklist on the dashboard, currently as a visual sample.
why: The code is a layout placeholder. The buttons are not connected to any saving or reading logic, which the file itself shows.
how: It holds a fixed list of three medicines with a time and a status. It draws each one as a card with a status color and a button, plus a fixed 'Remaining' count and a link to manage prescriptions. Nothing is saved when the button is pressed.
inputs: None. The medicines are written into the file.
outputs: A checklist card showing medicines, times, and status buttons.
risks: A patient could believe a medicine was taken or missed, based on fixed text, and the 'Remaining' count of two does not change. Missed doses are shown from invented data.
debug: If the list never changes, that is expected because the data is fixed. To make it real, the list must come from the backend and the buttons must save to it.
